pages.title: Jake Auchincloss for Congress
pages.text:
New leadership to lower costs for working families
## Join Team Jake’s re-election campaign!
or click here to contribute another amount
Bringing new, innovative leadership to Washington to lower costs for working families.
- Jake was born and raised in the Massachusetts Fourth Congressional District he now represents, the son of a surgeon and a scientist. They taught him the values of curiosity and integrity.
- After graduating from Harvard College, Jake joined the Marines. He commanded infantry in Afghanistan and special operations in Panama. He’s now a major in the reserves.
- Jake won election to the Newton City Council in 2015, was re-elected in 2017, and topped the ticket in 2019. He resigned in 2020 after his election to Congress. Jake also worked on housing and transportation at Liberty Mutual’s innovation lab.
- Now in Congress, Jake is working to put the pandemic behind us and a strong economy in front of us. He’s been called someone who can “make friends and influence enemies in Washington.” He’s been delivering results from day one as a member of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and as Vice Chairman of the Financial Services Committee.
- Jake lives in Newtonville with his wife, Michelle; their son, Teddy; their daughter, Grace; and their Labrador Retriever, Donut.
Meet Jake →
 ‘He’s doing a very good job,’ [Barney] Frank, who represented the 4th District from 1981 to 2013, said…‘He’s part of that mainstream Democratic majority that’s doing well with Nancy Pelosi’s leadership.’ 
— Business Insider
Read full article
## Let’s get to work.
I'm the father of two pandemic babies. I met both Teddy and Grace for the first time in surge-strained hospitals. One of Teddy’s first words was “mask.” My wife and I once assumed that neither of them would even remember COVID. Now we worry that it will cloud their childhood. I see our anxiety mirrored in my constituents, of all ages.
Like so many parents, this is not the path I want for my kids. Step one is the schools. Re-opening schools was my day-one priority when I took office in January 2021, and Congress sent more than $130 billion to school districts last winter to help them reopen. No school should be operating without high-quality ventilation and filtration systems. And, every school district should have clear, forward-looking infectious-disease policies that disavow closures and implement restrictions only as a last resort, with input from child psychologists and parents in addition to public health officials. If states and cities need more flexibility from American Rescue Plan funds to pandemic-proof their schools, then Congress must give it to them.
We must also expand youth services. Congress is working to guarantee affordable access to child care and early education for every family. Mental health should be part of that deal, too. But capping costs leads to shortages if we don’t simultaneously expand supply. There are too few pediatricians, inpatient providers, child psychologists, adjustment counselors, social workers, early educators, and childcare specialists. Boosting supply may require the government at all levels to cut red tape for occupational licensing, subsidize workforce education, increase funding for afterschool and other wraparound programming, and change rules for insurance rates. If states need more flexibility from American Rescue Plan funds to achieve this, then Congress must give it to them. Congress must also pass two bipartisan bills, both of which I have cosponsored, to (1) better fund children’s mental health, and (2) incorporate collaborative care models, which integrate mental health services with primary care.
I’ve only been a congressman for one year and a parent for two, but I am committed for the long haul to improving children’s socioemotional wellbeing. It’s a special responsibility I have as the youngest parent in the House Democratic caucus. COVID is a fork in the road: let’s take the harder, better path for our kids.
In Congress I am using every tool at my disposal to drive down costs for families. Rising costs, from housing to heating to child care, are a real problem. Pandemic and overseas war have primarily driven this inflation by disrupting supply chains and employment, but now Congress must help fix it. While Republicans were trying to use inflation for political points, I offered real solutions to get our economy back on track .
I am also fighting to lower or eliminate out-of-pocket costs in health care, so that patients never struggle to afford the medicines they need.
We must work across the government, business, and education sectors to boost employment and increase research and development. That is why I was proud to play a role in securing key wins in the House version of the COMPETES Act , a generational investment in our workforce, supply chains, and America’s leadership in science and technology.
As a member of the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee I am working to ensure that Massachusetts residents benefit from better infrastructure, which supports stronger towns and healthier families. In my first term I helped pass an historic, bipartisan infrastructure bill. Now, I’m working with state and local leaders as America invests more than $1T in roads and bridges, transit, high-speed internet, the electric grid, and clean water.
Climate change is a clear and present threat to our planet and our children’s way of life. Even before coming to Congress, I was leading on this issue in the private sector and in local government. On the city council, I voted with Green Newton priorities 100% of the time. At a Fortune 100, I helped build products for sustainable mobility. Leading environmental advocates endorsed me for Congress because they knew I’d hit the ground running – and I have. As an original co-sponsor of the Green New Deal and leading advocate for Offshore Wind, I have called for a carbon tax to curb the pollution that causes climate change; fought for investments in green infrastructure and clean-energy research and development; and have become a champion for sustainable, on-demand transit.
We must protect access to the ballot and the independence of state election officials. Our campaign is committed to fighting to protect our democracy. My work has won me the endorsement of the Progressive Turnout Project who cited my “history of championing pro-democracy legislation and a shared commitment to a reality that everyone has the right to vote in a country where voting is made simple and accessible to all.”

pages.title: Demilitarize the Police — Jake Auchincloss for Congress
pages.text:
## After 9/11, Policing Underwent Radical Change. It’s Time To Course Correct
Contrary to the president’s claims, the protests of the last weeks have been overwhelmingly peaceful. Yet, we see the tools of war on our streets. Police and the National Guard patrol with the weapons and armor that I recognize from my overseas deployments in the Marines.
We must demilitarize the police. To do this, we must shift the paradigm of public safety, at home and abroad.
After September 11th, government at all levels — federal, state, local — increasingly flipped the idea of policing on its head. State and local police were given more military and intelligence capabilities, while troops overseas were tasked with policing foreign soil.
The new Department of Homeland Security became a bridge between the two. From airports to subways to street corners, our everyday experience became marked by lurking threats that required overwhelming force. We were all deputized to "say something," if we "see something."
Conversely, our troops are deployed as police. That includes me. As an infantry platoon commander in Helmand Province, my mission was to patrol three villages subject to Taliban influence. In tandem with the Afghan police, we tried to establish rapport with tribal elders, to root out Taliban abettors and to generally underwrite security. Marines are expeditionary — we are meant to take on unfamiliar missions. But we are not police.
Our military is policing villages that are not their own, and our police are empowered to act with military force. These twin failed initiatives must stop: get the military and intelligence services out of our public square here at home, and stop using our military as a police force overseas. As monumental as ending the forever wars would be, it is the former — the demilitarization of police — that will be the harder call to action.
Each city and town can begin by looking at dispatches and details. How often are cops being asked to control traffic? Cite noise violators? Handle substance abuse? And, how often would recourse to force have been necessary to protect public safety?
As the chair of the public safety and transportation committee on the Newton City Council, I am helping to steer that review for my hometown. I expect we'll find that we're asking police to not just keep us safe from violent crime, but also to handle every other assignment that has rolled downhill from law to enforcement, without due consideration for the right agent to enforce.
In some cases, it's already obvious it's not working. For example: Newton police are being called on landscapers whose leaf blowers are too loud. By expanding the surface area of police-citizen contact into these types of non-threatening situations, we increase the likelihood of violence — especially violence predicated on racial profiling.
Race must be at the center of this review. Collecting data on policing and racism should become a national project, but we can’t let this be a statistics discussion when Black and brown voices on the subject have been clear for centuries: our fellow Americans do not trust law enforcement. As a white man, I feel safer when cops are nearby. Many of my Black and brown constituents do not, and for good reason.
Ending the 9/11 mindset, and reviewing police functions through the lens of racial justice, will be good for both citizens and police. To be sure, we need a public safety arm that can use force to protect people — nobody wants to dial 911 during a robbery and get a ringtone. But we have taken the right of government to use force and spread it across domains where force is rarely helpful.
I’m proud that we’re starting this conversation in my hometown’s City Hall, along with cities and towns throughout the United States. To complete it, though, will take action from Washington, too. Stop militarizing the police. And stop asking the military to police other peoples. From my patrol base in Helmand to my chair at the public safety committee, I know we can do better.

## February 22nd, 2020
Yesterday, Jake sat down with WCVB’s On the Record to discuss his campaign for Congress. He talked about what it’s going to take to tackle some of our biggest challenges — including climate change, a broken transportation system, healthcare, immigration, and endless wars abroad.

pages.title: Priorities — Jake Auchincloss for Congress
pages.text:
## Let’s get to work.
In the Marines, Jake worked with Americans of every color towards a common purpose. Diversity and inclusion weren't just core values; they were critical to mission success. As a city councilor, Jake continued to promote equity. Civil rights activists in Newton lauded his work at the intersection of housing and racial justice.
Congress must seize this moment of reckoning by:
- Strengthening the Voting Rights Act to end voter suppression
- Demilitarizing the police and reinstating consent decrees
- Funding housing, transit, education, job-training and public health to match the long-underserved needs of communities of color
- Closing the racial wealth gap and expanding opportunity for low-income children through baby bonds
Reproductive care is health care. Every woman deserves access to birth control and to safe and legal abortions. Jake is standing up to the GOP’s anti-choice agenda by
- Defending Title X and securing funding for Planned Parenthood
- Pushing for the elimination of the Hyde Amendment and the Global Gag Rule, and
- Working towards a ROE Bill of Rights
Jake has a track record of delivering progressive solutions to address climate change. On the city council, he voted with Green Newton priorities 100% of the time. At a Fortune 100, he helped build products for sustainable mobility. Leading environmental advocates endorsed him for Congress because he'll hit the ground running:
- Tax carbon to curb the pollution that causes climate change
- Invest in green infrastructure and clean-energy R&D. Fund the investments by cutting the Pentagon's budget by 10%
- Regain US global leadership on the climate crisis by recommitting to and then strengthening the Paris Agreement
- Create good jobs in green industries, including offshore wind
- Support Community Climate Justice, including Clean Water for All
As a Marine, Jake slept, ate, trained, and patrolled with an assault weapon for four years. Those weapons of war have no place on our streets or near our schools. As your congressman, Jake is standing up to the NRA to enact common-sense gun-safety legislation:
- Universal background checks
- Federal assault weapons ban & mandatory buyback
- Red Flag Laws to strengthen the Violence Against Women Act and prevent mass shootings
- Mandatory liability insurance for all firearms
- Violence intervention programs, informed by public health research, for communities plagued by gun violence
- Ending the gun-show and ghost-gun loopholes
Jake has worked at a startup and a Fortune 100. He's served in government and at a non-profit. And he has degrees in economics and finance. He's seen the Massachusetts economy from multiple angles – theory and practice, high-tech and Main Street. The common denominator is the talent of our people.
In an inclusive economy, everyone can realize their talent, provide for their families, and retire with dignity. In Congress, Jake will work for:
- Universal, high-quality pre-K, which he helped advance as a city councilor, and the Child Care is Infrastructure Act
- Expanded technical & vocational training and free community college
- Investments in infrastructure and basic research to boost productivity
- More high-paying jobs in southeastern Massachusetts, especially centered on advanced manufacturing
- Stronger unions, paid family & medical leave, and a $15 minimum wage
- Streamlined regulations and greater support for small businesses
- The restoration of defined benefit plans and the absolute protection of Social Security and Medicare
Jake has worked in transportation in government and business. He is now a member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee. The Future of Transportation Caucus's principles of access, equity, and sustainability guide his policy. He supports:
- Funding transit and highways equally, not 20/80
- Providing state & local agencies more funding to run buses and trains. Tying that funding to:
- criteria for transit-friendly streets & safe roadways for all users
- reductions in transportation emissions
- measurable improvements in connecting people to jobs & destinations
- Halting roadway expansion in order to prioritize the maintenance backlog, especially for bridges
- Improving airports and seaports, including the Port of New Bedford
- Expanding the national passenger rail system, including South Coast Rail
Every American deserves access to quality, affordable healthcare. In Congress, Jake supports the Biden administration's efforts to build on Obamacare through tax credits and a public option. He is also working to:
- Eliminate co-pays for prescription drugs
- Break up concentrations of market power that drive up prices
- Prevent Republicans from privatizing or cutting Medicare
- Support Massachusetts' world-leading life sciences ecosystem
Talent is everywhere, but opportunity is not. Jake’s great-grandparents fled the Russian pogroms and built a small business in Massachusetts. They came for the American promise: that the condition of your birth should not determine the circumstances of your life.
We fail that promise when we shut our doors to immigrants and refugees, or when we deprive those here of the same rights and opportunities as native-born Americans. We also deplete our economic and cultural richness.
As a Newton city councilor, Jake co-docketed the Welcoming City ordinance to protect immigrants from ICE overreach. As a congressman, Jake will work with President Biden to roll back Trump’s cruel and counterproductive immigration policies. America must once again be a nation of immigrants.
Jake commanded special operations and knows what the U.S. military is capable of—and what it is not. Congress must repeal the post-9/11 Authorization for Use of Military Force and end the failed Forever Wars. In tandem, Congress should use its power of the purse to direct the president to:
- Reduce the size of conventional ground forces and invest the savings in green infrastructure and clean-energy R&D
- Match naval, air, cyber, intelligence, and special operations capabilities to the imperatives to
- defend the U.S. homeland & strategic infrastructure
- safeguard allies and multilateral institutions
- protect the global commons
- contain Chinese influence in the Pacific theater, and
- intervene to stop humanitarian catastrophes
- Emphasize foreign aid, robust diplomacy, and U.S. leadership on transnational threats like climate change & pandemics over the projection of military might
Jake unequivocally supports military aid to Israel as negotiated in the Obama-era MOU and recognizes Jerusalem as the capital of Israel. He opposes the BDS movement. As a Jew and as an American, he is committed to Israel’s security and prosperity.
America’s alliance with Israel is based on shared values and shared interests. Israel shares our commitment to free and fair elections, individual rights, a free press, and an independent judiciary. Israel does not always live up to its highest ideals, but it remains committed to democracy despite decades of war and terrorism.
Jake supports the Abraham Accords, and he favors a two-state solution. He recognizes that it must be negotiated between the involved actors and cannot be imposed by outsiders. The solution must result in a viable state for the Palestinians and security for Israelis.
Read Jake’s Israel position paper here.
Read Jake’s AJC questionnaire here.
After the most corrupt presidency in U.S. history, Americans' trust in the rule of law is shaken. Congress must help restore it. Jake is committed to the legislative blueprint proposed by Protect Democracy .
The blueprint includes measures to strengthen Congress's powers over war, spending, nominations, and oversight; to codify checks on executive powers; and to protect the apolitical status of the courts and other independent institutions. Key elements are included in the "Protecting our Democracy Act,” which Jake supports.
Jake also supports independent redistricting commissions, campaign finance reform, and better enforcement of federal ethics and disclosure laws. Dig deeper into other dimensions of democracy reform here.

A new generation offering fresh, independent solutions
This moment demands leaders who focus on the next generation , not the next news cycle. Jake is a Marine veteran and the youngest Democratic parent in Congress. He is fighting the gun lobby to shield children from their leading cause of death. He is dedicated to protecting the Constitution and individual rights, including abortion rights. And he is fighting special interests to lower drug prices for seniors and the middle class. Jake is working on all fronts for the freedom, security, and success of every American.

Jake joins Fox News Live to discuss how Kamala Harris was in command, and Donald Trump was out of control during the presidential debate.

Jake joins WCVB's On The Record after the recent school shooting in Georgia to discuss the gun safety legislation needed to keep weapons of war out of our schools.

Ending Gun Violence
Jake slept, ate, trained, and patrolled with an assault weapon for 4 years as a Marine officer. He believes weapons of war have no place on our streets or near our schools, which is why he’s working for an assault-weapons ban and other common-sense gun safety measures.
Advancing Reproductive Freedom
With abortion access in jeopardy across the country, it’s more important than ever that we elect leaders who'll protect the freedom to choose. Jake was endorsed by the Planned Parenthood Action Fund as a strong advocate for reproductive health and abortion rights in Congress.
Upholding Democracy & U.S. Global Leadership
Democracy is under siege, at home and abroad. Jake’s first speech in Congress was to advocate impeaching Donald Trump, and he continues to fight Trumpism at every turn. Jake has also been one of the strongest congressional supporters of Ukraine, Israel, and Indo-Pacific allies in the global contest against tyranny, terror, and totalitarianism.

Climate change requires bold action to protect our planet and our children’s way of life. As a millennial & the youngest Democratic parent in Congress, Jake has a fierce sense of urgency to invest in clean energy and ensure clean air, clean water, and clean soil.

## Good leaders eat last
This administration's corruption and cronyism threaten the rule of law and make the American Dream impossibly expensive.
I work in Washington to defend democracy and to lower prices.
Democrats need big ideas. Americans do not trust either party. We cannot earn back their trust by defending the status quo. We must demonstrate that we can govern better, and better governance starts with better ideas. These ideas are not fine pottery to be admired, they are clay to be molded. Together.
Simple but Not Easy is dedicated to sharing ideas for us to shape together.
JAKE IN THE NEWS
Jake speaks directly to Donald Trump on Fox News
"I said it directly to Trump on Fox: you are the only president to start and lose a war by yourself."
Rep. Auchincloss: Won’t Fund ‘Illegal’ War
Jake joins Bloomberg to discuss how he will not vote “for a single dollar” to fund what he calls a failed and illegal war, arguing Congress must prevent it from becoming a “forever war.”
Democrat sounds off on ICE after deadly Minneapolis shooting: 'Instrument of fear'

pages.title: Issues — Jake Auchincloss for Congress
pages.text:
## Issues
I believe in equal opportunity for all and special privileges for none. I’m in Congress to deliver a New American Dream, in which working hard and following the rules secures an:
excellent education by 18;
a home of your own by 30; and
a dignified retirement by 65.
The foundation of this American Dream is the rule of law and individual freedom. Americans owe one another equal justice under law. And we commit to one another free minds, free enterprise, free elections, and freedom from fear.
Here’s what I’m working on:
## The financial freedom agenda
Treat cost disease, reduce the debt, and save Social Security
Americans deserve better than a hot-potato game of ‘affordability.’ In that game, whichever party is out of power promises to lower prices. Then, it fails to deliver.
Americans deserve financial freedom.
Treating cost disease
Cost disease is when prices in a sector go up faster than wages, year over year. Housing, healthcare, and utilities are most afflicted. But their cost disease can be treated. Cut regulations that drive up prices, like bans on starter homes. Promote technology that lowers prices, particularly in hospital services. And, always: take on special interests, like utilities, that keep prices high.
Saving Social Security
This earned benefit is sacrosanct. Yet, it’s on track to be insolvent by 2033. Congress must fix the arithmetic of Social Security. That fix should include the wealthiest paying more than into a Trust Fund. It should also include raising the minimum wage and expanding access to wealth creation for workers.
Reduce the debt
The last president to balance the budget was a Democrat, and the next one should be, too. Handing off more than $40 trillion in debt to the next generation is a bill that comes due in taxes and inflation. It’s not fair.
Lowering deficits requires changes in growth, taxes and spending. Education, science, infrastructure and legal immigration improvements drive growth. Closing tax preferences like the Buy-Borrow-Die loophole for billionaires will raise tax revenue. And pursuing efficiencies in healthcare delivery, especially in chronic-disease care, can lower spending.
A congressman on how Democrats can regain the initiative on the economy ( The Economist )
Cost disease: what it is & why it matters ( Simple but Not Easy )
Lower prices or perish ( Simple but Not Easy )
Save Social Security & the 3-leg stool (Simple but Not Easy)
## Social media & AI regulation
Social media corporations are running an experiment on our children for profit
The results are devastating for families. The typical American child now spends less time outdoors than a federal inmate.
In 2024, I co-led legislation to force TikTok out from under the Chinese Communist Party.
Now I’m leading legislation in Congress to:
Raise the minimum age for social media accounts from 13 to 16 - Social media and similar apps must verify users’ ages without uploading photo IDs or scanning faces.
Hold social media & AI companies liable for deepfakes, harassment, and other harms.
Tax Big Tech – which pays lower effective rates than most nurses – to fund the construction of 1,000 trade schools and to surge 1:1 tutoring to public schools. After the catastrophic school closures, American public school students need more help.
Digital Dopamine Is Consuming America. It’s Time to Fight for IRL. (The New York Times)
Touch Grass Populism (Simple but Not Easy)
## The Eds & Meds economy in Massachusetts
Medical science delivers therapies for dread diseases like cancer, Alzheimer’s, and addiction. It’s also a jobs engine for Massachusetts. Every 10 biotech hires generates 16 non-biotech jobs.
Yet science is under attack right now.
Bloomberg called me the “Democrat taking on RFK Jr.” I fight his quackery, grift and incompetence. I am also leading legislation to:
Fix affordability and access in drug pricing . Patients should pay low or no co-pays. Insurance companies must not abuse prior authorization. And American patients should always get the newest, life-saving medicines.
Support and defend the integrity of the National Institutes of Health and the Food & Drug Administration. Peer review, not politics, should determine which science is funded. Medicines should be evaluated based on safety & efficacy, not wins for the White House.
Modernize U.S. clinical trials infrastructure. Better and faster trials will reduce the cost of drug development, bring therapies to market faster, and make the United States more competitive versus China.
Auchincloss Calls FDA Voucher Program ‘Illegal,’ Warns of Political Pressure (Inside Health Policy)
America versus Alzheimer's (Simple but Not Easy)
(The Boston Globe)
## Support & defense of the rule of law
Corruption is out of control. It’s not just Trump, with his crypto scams and slush funds for friends & felons. It’s a political system in which dark money floods elections, lawmakers don’t listen, and authoritarian actions go unpunished.
Overturn Citizens United . Mine was the first signature on a ballot petition in Massachusetts to overturn this Supreme Court decision. It unleashed dark money and corporate contributions in elections. I’ll continue working to clean up that mess.
Ban government officials from stock trading , prediction markets, and cryptocurrencies. Elected officials should also submit annual cognitive exams for the public record.
Restore checks & balances . Strengthen congressional control over war, tariffs, appropriations, law enforcement, and independent agencies.
The rule of law is not only about the Constitution. It’s also about public safety. When shampoo is locked up, but not shoplifters, then public order decays. Public safety policy should prosecute those who break the law with firmness and justice. It should train and resource the police to solve crimes at a higher rate. And it should integrate behavioral and addiction services.
This Democrat Thinks Voters Seeking Order Will Make or Break Elections (The Wall Street Journal)
Rep. Jake Auchincloss is a Massachusetts Democrat with centrist appeal (The Washington Post)
How Dems can deliver law & order (Simple but Not Easy)
Democrats need big ideas. Americans do not trust either party. We cannot earn back their trust by defending the status quo. We must demonstrate that we can govern better, and better governance starts with better ideas. These ideas are not fine pottery to be admired, they are clay to be molded. Together.
Simple but Not Easy is dedicated to sharing ideas for us to shape together.

pages.title: Achieving a Clean Energy Future
pages.text:
## Achieving a Clean Energy Future
Climate change requires bold action to protect our planet and our children’s way of life. As a millennial & the youngest Democratic parent in Congress, Jake has a fierce sense of urgency to invest in clean energy and to ensure clean air, clean water, and clean soil.
Jake strongly supported the Inflation Reduction Act , the biggest & boldest climate action & clean energy investment in history, in his first term in Congress. Since then, he’s been partnering with public & private officials to advance clean-energy solutions, from fission & fusion to offshore wind to hot-rock geothermal, while building environmental resilience through civil engineering projects throughout the district.
Jake has also been a strong proponent of the land use & transportation changes that reduce cities’ carbon footprint and improve walkability, like Complete Streets policies for cycling & walking; liberalizing zoning for multi-family & mixed-use development; and transit improvements.

pages.title: Advancing Reproductive Freedom
pages.text:
## Advancing Reproductive Freedom
With abortion access in jeopardy across the country, it’s more important than ever that we elect leaders who'll protect the freedom to choose. Jake was endorsed by the Planned Parenthood Action Fund as a strong advocate for reproductive health and rights in Congress.
The Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade undermined women's right to control their own bodies and their own lives. With the Court failing to protect women's freedom, the U.S. House and Senate must step up and make Roe the law of the land – which is one reason Jake has advocated eliminating the filibuster.
While we fight for reproductive freedom everywhere, abortion remains legal in Massachusetts, and federal & state officials are working together to provide reproductive health care in Massachusetts for women in states that ban it.

pages.title: Ending Gun Violence
pages.text:
## Ending Gun Violence
Jake slept, ate, trained, and patrolled with an assault weapon for 4 years as a Marine officer. He believes weapons of war have no place on our streets or near our schools, which is why he’s working for an assault-weapons ban and other common-sense gun safety measures.
In addition to fighting for an assault weapons ban, Jake’s gun-safety priorities include:
Universal background checks to prevent criminals from buying weapons
Mandatory safe storage to protect children from their leading cause of death
Stricter enforcement of ghost gun provisions to prevent strong state laws, like those in Massachusetts, from being undermined by online retailers
Red flag laws to disarm those who are imminently a threat to themselves or others
Overturning the 2005 law that granted gun manufacturers immunity from liability, shielding them from lawsuits and stalling the adoption of safety devices
Jake's work in Congress has earned him the Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate Distinction and Brady PAC's endorsement.

pages.title: Strengthening the Middle Class
pages.text:
## Strengthening the Middle Class
High costs, from housing & healthcare to child care & college, are destabilizing the U.S. middle class. Millennials are not as economically secure as their parents were at this stage in their life. Drawing on his economics and business background, Jake has consistently offered policies, not talking points, to address the cost of living.
When Republicans were trying to use inflation for political points, Jake offered real solutions to get our economy back on track . Pointing to the cost of housing as the Bay State’s biggest problem, Jake has also consistently worked for pro-housing policies at all levels of government, from the Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act in Congress to the MBTA Communities Act on Beacon Hill.
As a Member of the Transportation & Infrastructure Committee, Jake has worked to improve supply chains and to pass the landmark Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and CHIPS & Science Act , which will improve the building blocks of the economy, from roads & bridges to science to workforce training.

pages.title: Taking on Special Interests: Lower Rx Prices
pages.text:
## Taking on Special Interests: Lower Rx Prices
Jake stood up to special interests and helped pass legislation to empower Medicare to negotiate drug prices and to cap out-of-pocket costs for seniors. Now, he’s working to extend & deepen those benefits.
By taking on the greed of the big health insurance companies, Jake is fighting to cap out-of-pocket costs for all Americans.
When a physician prescribes a drug that you need to get healthy, insurance companies shouldn’t be able to shift cost and friction onto you to prevent access to that medication. But that’s exactly what’s happening: drug-pricing middlemen, known as pharmacy benefit managers, are denying access to patients and making independent pharmacists miserable while raking in billions of profit every year for their insurance-company owners.
Jake is moving multiple pieces of legislation, much of it bipartisan, to take on the insurance companies to lower prescription drug costs for patients. He is also a leader in pushing for adoption of innovative pricing models for a new era of cell-and-gene engineering and other personalized therapies.

pages.title: Upholding Democracy & U.S. Global Leadership
pages.text:
## Upholding Democracy & U.S. Global Leadership
Democracy is under attack, at home and abroad.
Jake’s first speech in Congress was to advocate impeaching Donald Trump, and he continues to fight Trumpism at every turn. Jake has also been one of the strongest congressional supporters of Ukraine, Israel, and Indo-Pacific allies in the global contest against tyranny, terror, and totalitarianism.
As a member of the House Select Committee on Strategic Competition between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, Jake has pressed for U.S. investments in science, education and infrastructure as the surest means of outcompeting the Chinese Communist Party. On the Financial Services committee, he was one of the earliest proponents of energy sanctions on Russia, which the administration has since employed. And Jake has been a strong defender of Israel’s right to protect its citizens against terrorist attacks.
Support for democracies overseas must be matched by support for democracy at home. Jake has consistently pointed out that Xi Jinping’s best day in office was January 6, 2021 – and that the greatest threat to the United States is no foreign power, but the specter of another Trump term and the disaster that would entail for the rule of law and the Constitution.
To improve the integrity of U.S. politics, Jake is a supporter of legislation to end the distortions of dark money, gerrymandering, and stock-trading by members. He is also in favor of term limits and an enforceable code of ethics for the Supreme Court.
